artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

artifacts.title: Nickoley and Stephens v. Southwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Bruce Nickoley and David Stephens complained against Southwest Presbytery's actions in withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving a pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of a local church session. The SJC denied the complaint, affirming that the Presbytery correctly determined it lacked constitutional authority to suspend the session or act as a 'Session pro tem' without congregational consent, and that original jurisdiction over charges against ruling elders rested with the local session.

artifacts.title: Re-examination of previously ordained officer nominees by session
artifacts.disposition: advice given — re-examination required; session may find nominee deficient

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that all nominees for ruling elder or deacon, including previously ordained individuals, must be re-examined by the session, which retains the right to find them deficient.

artifacts.title: Re-examination and divestiture of officers in rotational systems

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that the BCO provides no procedure for re-examining rotated-off officers' qualifications, but divestiture may only occur under BCO 24-6, 38-2, or 34-10.

artifacts.title: Session authority over officer nominees and inactive elders under rotation

matches.evidence: A session must present all qualified nominees for election and may not use BCO 24-6 to exclude inactive officers; presbytery proceedings are not automatically required for long-inactive elders.

artifacts.title: Teaching elder voting rights and congregational approval of pastoral salary changes

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that a teaching elder votes as a full session member, and that any change to pastoral salary terms requires congregational approval as part of the call.

artifacts.title: Whether congregation may dissolve the session by vote

matches.evidence: A congregation cannot dissolve the session; it may by majority vote request individual officer removals under BCO 24-6, but the final decision rests with the session, and presbytery may assume jurisdiction under BCO 13-9.
